classification.difficultyReason: Find the radius from the diameter, subtract four circle areas from a rectangle, and substitute the specified approximation for pi.

content.prompt: Four coins, each with diameter $2\text{ cm}$, are cut from a metal rectangle with side lengths that are $10\text{ cm}$ and $5\text{ cm}$, as shown below. What is the remaining area? Give your answer in terms of $\pi$ and then find an approximate value using $\pi\approx\frac{22}{7}$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, rectangle and four coins below the stem
spec.description: Unshaded 10 cm by 5 cm rectangle containing four separate equal circles. Their centres retain the source positions: upper left, upper middle-right, lower middle and lower right. The lower-middle circle has a complete sloping diameter labelled 2 cm. Ordinary blue outlines and red centre markers are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle dimensions 10 cm and 5 cm; four circles each of diameter 2 cm. The indicated diameter passes through its circle centre and terminates on both sides of the circumference.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and centre markers are visible; no calculated radius or area is shown.

answer.short:
$(50-4\pi)\text{ cm}^2$; approximately $37\frac{3}{7}\text{ cm}^2$.

Subtract the areas of the four coins from the rectangle.
